The notes of every release, as published on
[GitHub](https://github.com/NikoBiele/convinterp/releases), newest first. The wheels of each
release are on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/convinterp/), and each release is archived on
Zenodo under its own DOI; the citation file in the repository has the details.

## [v0.2.0](https://github.com/NikoBiele/convinterp/releases/tag/v0.2.0) — 2026-09-26

Integrals of any order, in 1D and N-D.

##### New

- **Integrals.** A negative `derivative` order gives the integral of the interpolant: `derivative=-1` is the antiderivative, `-2` the twofold integral, and so on, up to order 8 for `"b7"` to `"b13"`. Each integral is anchored at the first knot, where it and all lower integrals are zero.
- **Mixed orders in N-D.** Integrals can be combined with values and derivatives, one order per axis, e.g. `derivative=(-1, 1)`.
- **Fast and exact.** Integrals are computed exactly from the kernels' polynomial pieces, converge at the kernel's interpolation order, and evaluate in constant time per point, about as fast as the interpolant itself.
- **Documentation.** An Integrals section in the user guide, a theory section on how integrals work, integral convergence and speed on the accuracy page, and a new Limitations section.

##### Breaking changes

None.

##### Migration guide

No changes needed. Negative derivative orders, which previously raised a `ValueError`, now return integrals.

## [v0.1.1](https://github.com/NikoBiele/convinterp/releases/tag/v0.1.1) — 2026-09-26

Bug-fix release.

##### Fixes

- Knots containing NaN or infinity are now rejected with a `ValueError`. Previously a NaN inside the grid passed the uniformity check and gave silently wrong results.
- `bc="quadratic"` with only 2 data values along an axis now raises a `ValueError`, instead of an internal Rust panic (`PanicException`), for every kernel from `a3` up.

##### Breaking changes

None.

##### Migration guide

No changes needed. Code that passed non-finite knots, or `bc="quadratic"` with only 2 values, now gets a clear `ValueError`.

## [v0.1.0](https://github.com/NikoBiele/convinterp/releases/tag/v0.1.0) — 2026-09-26

First alpha release of convinterp, a Python port of ConvolutionInterpolations.jl with a Rust core.

- Interpolation on uniform grids in any number of dimensions
- Derivatives, with a derivative order per axis, up to each kernel's highest order
- Kernels a0 to a7 and b5 to b13, boundary conditions poly, linear, quadratic and detect
- Wheels for Linux, macOS and Windows on x86_64 and ARM

#### Breaking changes

None: this is the first release.

#### Migration guide

Not applicable: this is the first release.
